question.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}\{v,w\}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 5 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
